pages.title: What Is Waste?
pages.content:
Every day, we use many things. We eat food, drink from plastic or glass bottles, and have a lot of paper boxes and plastic packages. After that, we often throw them away. This is waste. Waste is anything that we don't want or need anymore.

Today, the world makes a lot of waste. In 2023, people in cities made more than 2 billion tons of waste. By 2050, this number may be nearly 4 billion tons. That is a very big problem.

Most of the waste in cities is food. Paper, boxes and plastic come next. Plastic waste is growing very fast, and a lot of it goes into rivers and seas.

But waste is not only a problem. Many things in our trash are still useful. We can collect them and use them again. Different kinds of waste need different ways of collecting and recycling.

vocabulary.definition: Things that people throw away because they don't need them.
To put something in the trash.
A unit for weighing very heavy things.
Things that you throw away.
To bring things together in one place.
Making new things from old, used things.

pages.title: Paper, Wood and Glass
pages.content:
Paper comes from trees in forests. When we recycle paper, we need fewer new trees. Paper waste must stay dry, so people collect it in a separate bin. In recycling centers, old paper becomes new paper and new boxes.

Wood also comes from trees. We use it for furniture, boxes and houses. Recycling centers can change old wood into new boards. Then people can use it again and don't have to throw it away.

Glass is made from sand and some other natural materials. Old bottles and jars are glass waste. People put them in special glass bins. Workers sort the glass by color. Then they melt it and make new bottles and jars. This saves natural materials and keeps the air cleaner.

vocabulary.definition: Not together with other things.
A large box for trash.
A place where old things become new materials.
A long, flat piece of wood.
A glass container for food, like honey or jam.
To put things into groups.
To make something hot until it becomes liquid.

pages.title: Plastic
pages.content:
Plastic is everywhere. We find it in bags, bottles, toys, phones and many other things. But there are many kinds of plastic, so we can't recycle all of them in the same way.

Between 2000 and 2019, the world made almost twice as much plastic. Plastic waste grew even faster. In 2019, the world had about 350 million tons of plastic waste.

What happened to all this plastic waste? People recycled only 9 percent of it. They burned 19 percent in special places. Half of it went into landfills. Landfills are big places where people put trash under the ground. The other 22 percent stayed in open places or went into nature. A lot of it went into rivers and seas.

That is why plastic waste is a very big problem today.

vocabulary.definition: A light, strong material. We make bags and bottles from it.
Two times more.
A part of 100. 50 percent is half.
To destroy something with fire.
A big place where trash goes under the ground.
Trees, rivers, seas, animals and plants.

pages.title: Cartons and Metal
pages.content:
Juice and milk cartons are made of paper and plastic together. Some also have a very thin layer of metal. This kind of packaging is very common, so it makes a lot of waste. People must collect it separately. Special centers separate the paper from the plastic. Then they use these materials to make new products.

Metal comes from the ground. Drink cans, oil cans and tomato paste cans are metal waste. People collect metal separately, too. In recycling centers, workers melt the old metal and make new things from it.

Is recycling metal a good idea? Yes, it is! It uses much less energy than taking new metal from the earth.

vocabulary.definition: A box made of paper and plastic. Milk and juice come in it.
Boxes, bags and bottles around the things we buy.
Not together with other things.
Something that people make and sell.
A metal container for drinks or food.
Power from electricity, gas or oil. Machines need it to work.

pages.title: Cooking Oil and Food
pages.content:
We make cooking oil from plants like olives, sunflowers and corn. After we fry food, we have used oil. Old oil is waste, too. It can make our water dirty, so we must collect it separately. Special centers change it into a clean fuel for cars and trucks. This fuel is called biodiesel.

Food waste comes from fruit and vegetable pieces, old bread and other food. Farms also have plant waste, like wheat and barley straw.

A lot of food never reaches our tables. About 13 percent of the world's food is lost on the way from the farm to the shop. Then 17 percent more is wasted in homes, restaurants and shops. And most food waste, 61 percent, happens at home!

vocabulary.definition: To cook food in hot oil.
Something that burns and gives energy, like gas.
A clean fuel made from plant oil.
The dry part of plants like wheat.
Gone. You can't use it anymore.
Not used and thrown away.

pages.title: Electronics and Batteries
pages.content:
We use many electronic items at home, at school and at work. Fridges, washing machines, computers and mobile phones make our lives easier. When they are old or broken, they become electronic waste. Electronic waste has dangerous materials in it, so we must put it in special bins. Workers take the old machines apart. Then they can use the metal, plastic and other useful parts again.

Batteries keep energy and give power to many things. When a battery is old or broken, it becomes battery waste. Never throw batteries in the normal trash! They have dangerous chemicals in them. These chemicals can get into the soil and water. We must put old batteries in battery bins. Then special centers take out useful metals like lithium, cobalt and nickel.

Recycling saves many useful materials. But it also needs a lot of energy and hard work. So recycling alone can't solve the problem. We need a better idea. This idea is Zero Waste.

vocabulary.definition: Working with electricity, like a computer or a phone.
It can hurt people or nature.
To separate something into small pieces.
A small object that gives power to things like phones.

The top part of the ground. Plants grow in it.

pages.title: What Is Zero Waste?
pages.content:
Does "zero waste" mean "no waste at all"? No, that isn't possible. We all use things and make waste every day.

Zero Waste is a way of living. It means using things carefully and making less trash. We try not to make waste. We use things again and again, and we recycle. With Zero Waste, we think about the whole life of a product. Then we understand that old things can still be valuable.

Every year, people make more than 2 billion tons of waste. A lot of this waste is still useful. When we throw it away, we lose it. Waste also makes the air, water and soil dirty. It is bad for our health and for nature.

vocabulary.definition: To find an answer to a problem.
The number 0. Nothing.
Thinking about what you do. Not quickly or badly.
Useful or important.
How well your body is.

pages.title: The Circular Economy
pages.content:
Zero Waste helps us build a circular economy. But first, let's look at the old way.

The old way is like a line. It has three steps: take, make, throw away. First, we take materials from nature. Then we make things from them. Finally, we throw them away. This is called a linear economy.

A circular economy is different. It works like a circle. In nature, nothing is wasted. Everything is used again and again. A circular economy works in the same way. We use products and materials for as long as possible. Then old things become new things. They go round and round in a circle, and they don't go to landfills.

The main goal is simple. The economy can grow, but nature doesn't have to pay for it.

vocabulary.definition: The money, work and business of a country.
Like a circle.
Like a straight line.
One part of a plan or job.
Something that you want to do.
To become bigger.

pages.title: The Three Rs
pages.content:
Zero Waste has three main rules. We call them the three Rs.

Reduce: Use less. Buy only the things that you really need.

Reuse and Repair: Use things again and again. Don't throw them away. Companies should make strong products, and these products should be easy to repair. When something breaks, fix it. Then it lasts longer, and you save money, too.

Recycle and Upcycle: Recycling means making new materials from old ones. For example, old paper becomes new paper. This saves natural materials, and less trash goes to landfills. Upcycling means making something new and more valuable from waste.

The circular economy is good for us in three ways. First, there is less waste and pollution. Second, we use natural materials better. Third, the economy grows, and there are new jobs in recycling and repair.

vocabulary.definition: To make something smaller or less.
To use something again.
To fix something that is broken.
To continue to work for a time.
To make something better from old things.
Dirty air, water or soil.

pages.title: Waste and Our Climate
pages.content:
Waste and climate change are connected. Food and other natural waste go bad in landfills. Then they give off a gas called methane. Methane is a greenhouse gas. Greenhouse gases make the Earth warmer.

Greenhouse gases in the world are more than twice as much as 50 years ago. Zero Waste can help. When we keep waste out of landfills, we make fewer of these bad gases.

Better waste management can cut these gases by 15 to 20 percent. But there is a big problem. Many poorer countries make very little of these gases. But they often suffer the most from climate change. They have terrible disasters, and the sea is rising there.

vocabulary.definition: Changes in the weather of the Earth over a long time.
To become old and not good to eat.
A gas in the air. It makes the Earth warmer.
Collecting, recycling and getting rid of waste.
To have pain or problems.
A very bad event, like a flood or a storm.
Things from nature, like wood or metal. We make products from them.

pages.title: What Can We Do?
pages.content:
The best waste is the waste that we never make. So we must act before there is any waste.

We can buy only the food that we need. We can shop at local markets and in shops without packaging. We can say "no" to things that we use only once. Paper coffee cups, plastic water bottles and plastic straws are good examples. There are better choices, like our own cups and bottles.

Cities can help, too. They can have places where people refill their drink bottles. They can have second-hand shops for clothes, furniture and electronics. They can also help people repair things. Some cities have tool libraries. People can borrow tools there, so they don't need to buy them.

Children and their families can learn about Zero Waste together. This is the best way to change our habits. And the best time to start is now!

Zero Waste is not a place where we arrive and stop. It is a way of thinking, and the journey never ends.
